metaDescription: Six Greenworks cordless string trimmers across the 24V, 40V and 60V platforms, compared on swath, line, weight, battery and which voltage suits your yard.
expertTake: The 60V 16 inch brushless is the best Greenworks trimmer for big or rough ground, and the 24V 13 inch brushless with a 4.0Ah battery is the best all-rounder for ordinary lawns. The 40V 15 inch is the value pick with a variable trigger. Anyone who does not already own that maker's batteries should compare the platform, not just the trimmer.
introParagraphs: A single garden-tool maker can offer string trimmers on four battery platforms, and picking the wrong one means buying batteries twice. The lighter systems suit small lawns and beginners, while the higher-voltage lines suit big properties and heavier line.
This guide climbs the range from the smallest system to the largest and shows where each step buys you something real: swath width, line size, brushless motors or a longer runtime.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 13 in. Brushless 2-in-1 String Trimmer and Edger, 4.0Ah
products.description:
This is the best balance of weight, power and battery in the range. A brushless motor drives a 13 inch cutting path with 0.080 inch line, which is heavier than the 0.065 inch line on most 24V trimmers, and an auto-feed system keeps the line advancing without bumping. A 4.0Ah battery is included, which is large for the 24V platform.

It converts easily between trimmer and edger, so one tool covers the lawn edge and the pavement edge. The 24V platform is the lightest in the brand's line, so the tool is easy to carry and use for a long session, and the brushless motor holds speed better than a brushed one as the pack runs down.

The limits are the platform and the thin single line: it is not a brush cutter. For regular lawn care on a medium lot it is exactly right. Clean the head after each use, replace the line when it gets short and store the battery indoors in winter. A 4.0Ah pack on a 13 inch head is a comfortable match, so you will usually finish a medium lot with charge to spare. If you later add a blower or hedge trimmer on the same platform, the pack carries over.
products.bestFor: Ordinary lawns on a medium lot that need trimming and edging.
pros: 0.080 in. line is heavier than most 24V tools
cons: Single line is not for brush

products.name: Greenworks 60V 16 in. Brushless String Trimmer, 2.5Ah, 6,000 RPM
products.description:
The 60V trimmer is the heaviest-duty machine the brand sells, and it is built to replace a gas trimmer. A 16 inch swath, dual 0.095 inch line and a brushless motor rated up to 6,000 RPM are the figures behind the maker's claim of 26cc gas-class power.

Its best feature is the reload. The head twists open and takes new line in about ten seconds with no winding, which the maker contrasts with a bump feed head, and fast reloading is what makes a thick line usable. The line is the heaviest in the range.

The cost is weight and a modest 2.5Ah pack, so a large property needs a second battery. The 60V pack is shared with the brand's other 60V tools, such as the blower in the combo kit. Use it for ditches, fences and overgrowth, and clean the head after each session. Work at about half throttle on open grass and save the full trigger for thick patches, since the pack drains quickly at full power. It is a tool for owners who have been disappointed by lighter trimmers and want something closer to a gas machine.
products.bestFor: Overgrown ground, fence lines and large properties.
pros: 16 inch swath with 0.095 in. dual line
cons: 2.5Ah pack is small for the swath

products.name: Greenworks 40V 15 in. TORQDRIVE String Trimmer, 0.085 in. Dual Line, 2.0Ah
products.description:
This 40V model is the best value for a larger lawn. A 15 inch dual-line head with 0.085 inch line sits between the 24V and 60V models, and the TORQDRIVE system provides, according to the maker, 30 percent more torque than a standard drive. A variable speed trigger lets you slow the head around plants.

The head is a bump feed, so you tap it on the ground to advance line, which is simple and robust but wastes line on hard surfaces. The pack is a 2.0Ah battery in the kit, small for a 15 inch swath, so a spare is a sensible purchase.

The 40V line is the brand's older platform, with a wide range of batteries and tools sold over the years, so spares are easy to find. Keep the head free of wrapped grass and tap on soft ground only. The variable trigger is worth learning to use, because a head at half speed throws far less debris at window glass and plants. Treat the TORQDRIVE claim as a helpful relative figure, not an absolute power rating.
products.bestFor: Mid to large lawns and buyers who want trigger control.
pros: Variable speed trigger for precise control
cons: 2.0Ah pack is small for this head
Bump feed wastes line on hard ground

products.name: Greenworks 40V 13 in. 2-in-1 Trimmer and Edger, 7.8 lb, 40 to 52 in. Shaft
products.description:
The distinctive feature is the head: it switches modes in three clicks and has seven pivot positions, which you move from trimming under decks at position 1 to edging sidewalks at position 3, clearing fence lines at position 5 and detailing flower beds at position 7. A steel edging guide is included for crisp lawn borders.

The shaft adjusts from 40 to 52 inches to fit users from about 5 feet 2 inches to 6 feet 4 inches, and the maker lists a weight of 7.8 pounds with anti-vibration technology. At that weight it is not the lightest, but the adjustability reduces back strain.

A 2.0Ah battery and charger are included. The 0.065 inch line suits lawn edges and light weeds. If edging is your main chore, the pivot and edging guide are the reason to choose this model. Set the shaft so your elbows are slightly bent and the head sits flat on the ground, then check the pivot position before you start each task. The seven positions are only useful if you actually change them, so learn which one suits each job.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who edge often and need an adjustable fit.
pros: Seven pivot positions for different tasks

products.name: Greenworks 24V 12 in. Brushless 2-in-1 Trimmer and Edger, 3.0Ah, Telescoping Shaft

specList.label: Shaft
specList.value: Telescoping aluminium, fits 4 ft 8 to 6 ft 5

products.description:
This 24V kit has a telescoping aluminium shaft that suits users from 4 feet 8 inches to 6 feet 5 inches, which covers nearly every adult in a household. A brushless motor drives a 12 inch cutting path with 0.065 inch dual line, and the head converts between trimmer and edger.

A 3.0Ah battery is included, a little less than the 4.0Ah on the 13 inch brushless model, but enough for a small to medium lawn. It makes a good family tool, since one person can set the shaft to their height in a few seconds.

The thinner line and smaller swath make it a tool for light growth. Wipe the telescoping joint after use and keep the pack indoors in winter. If you already have a 24V mower or blower from the brand, the pack is shared, which makes the kit cheaper than it looks. Teach everyone who uses it to lock the shaft collar firmly, since a loose collar is the one thing that spoils a shared tool.
products.bestFor: Households with users of different heights.
pros: Telescoping shaft fits 4 ft 8 to 6 ft 5

products.name: Greenworks 40V 12 in. BST4000 String Trimmer, Tool Only, Variable Trigger
products.description:
The BST4000 is the plain 40V trimmer for owners of the battery already. A 12 inch cutting path with 0.065 inch line and an auto feed head do the work, and a variable speed trigger lets you control the head as you move around plants.

The listing gives an operating temperature range, which is a useful detail for cold-climate owners, since lithium packs and plastic gears behave differently at low temperatures. It is a tool-only listing, so a battery and charger must be bought separately unless you have them from a mower or blower.

It is the cheapest way into the 40V trimmer line if you own packs, and a poor choice if you do not. Clean the head after each use and keep the pack indoors. A tool without a battery in the box is cheap only if you own the right pack, so check the platform before you order. If you do not own 40V packs, one of the 24V kits will cost less to start and weigh less in the hand.
products.bestFor: Owners of 40V Greenworks batteries who need a simple trimmer.
pros: Cheapest 40V trimmer if you own packs

buyingCriteria.explanation: The brand's trimmers sit on 24V, 40V and 60V platforms, and the packs are not interchangeable. The 24V models are lightest and the 60V model is heaviest. If you already own a battery from the brand, the right trimmer is the one that fits it. A household with a 40V mower should look at the 40V trimmers first, and one with a 60V blower at the 60V. Buying a new platform just for a trimmer is the most expensive way to get a string trimmer.

The 60V cuts 16 inches with 0.095 inch line, the 40V TORQDRIVE 15 inches with 0.085 inch, the 40V 2-in-1 13 inches, the 24V 13 inches with 0.080 inch and the 12 inch models use 0.065 inch. Heavier line cuts tougher growth, but it needs more torque and a head built for it. Do not fit thick line to a head rated for thin line, because it jams in the eyelets and overloads the motor.

The 24V and 60V models listed here are brushless, while the 40V models are not described that way. Brushless runs cooler and holds speed as the pack drains. For a small lawn it is a luxury, for large ones a benefit. The gain is mostly runtime and fewer parts to wear, so count it as a long-term saving and not a performance jump.

The 24V 13 inch and BST4000 use auto feed, the 40V TORQDRIVE uses bump feed and the 60V uses a twist reload. Auto feed is the easiest, twist reload is fastest for heavy line and bump feed is the simplest. Pick the one whose annoyance you can tolerate, since a feed system you dislike is the part of the trimmer you will resent most.

The 40V 2-in-1 weighs 7.8 pounds and adjusts 40 to 52 inches, and the 24V 12 inch fits users from 4 ft 8 to 6 ft 5. A tool that fits your body is easier to use than a lighter one that does not. Fit matters most when more than one person uses the trimmer, so pay for adjustability in a shared household.

The 24V 13 inch includes 4.0Ah, the 12 inch 3.0Ah, the 40V models 2.0Ah and the 60V 2.5Ah. A bigger pack matters more on bigger swaths, so plan a spare for 15 and 16 inch heads. A small pack on a wide head drains quickly and leaves you waiting at the charger, which is the most common regret among owners of the bigger models.

specDecoder.meaning: A drive system the maker says provides 30% more torque. It helps the head keep turning in thick growth.
A motor with electronic switching and no brushes.
A marketing comparison to an engine size.
The diameter of the cutting line. Heavier cuts tougher growth.
A trigger that sets head speed by how far you squeeze it. It lets you slow the head around plants and save charge on easy grass, which a fixed-speed trigger cannot do.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 24V, 40V and 60V options and the packs included. The 24V 13 inch and 60V scored well for their classes. We checked that each platform has a spare pack readily on sale, since a trimmer is only as good as the battery you can buy for it in year five.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared swath, line and motor type. The 60V led and the 24V brushless scored well for light work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at triggers, adjustable shafts and weights. The 40V 2-in-1 and the telescoping 24V scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Kit contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted batteries and chargers. The 4.0Ah 24V kit scored best and the bare BST4000 lowest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered parts and platform breadth. The brand's wide battery range scored well. Replacement spools and heads are stocked widely, which keeps the tools serviceable for years.

cards.label: 24V
cards.text: The 12 inch and 13 inch trimmers are lightest and brushless. They suit ordinary lawns.

cards.label: 40V and 60V
cards.text: The 40V models and the 60V have wider swaths and heavier line. They suit larger or rougher ground.

howToChoose.note: Choose 24V for ordinary lawns and 60V for anything rough.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a pivot head with several positions and an edging guide. Edging wears line fast, so an auto feed or fast reload helps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 40V 13 in. 2-in-1 offers seven pivot positions and a steel guide, and the 24V 13 in. converts easily with auto feed.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your ground is rough or your lawn large. The Greenworks 60V is the strongest.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you own 40V batteries. The BST4000 is the cheapest route.

maintenance.why: Packed grass strains the motor and bearing. Clear it with the battery removed.
Short line cuts a narrow swath. Use the diameter the head is rated for.
Grit stiffens the pivot and telescoping joints and stops them locking firmly. Wipe and brush them clean, and add a drop of dry lubricant to the telescoping tubes.
Cold lowers capacity, so keep them at half charge indoors.
A bent guide gives a wavy edge and lets the line cut into paving. Straighten or replace it.

faq.a: 24V for ordinary lawns, 40V for larger lawns and 60V for rough ground. If you own a battery, buy the matching trimmer.
No. 24V, 40V and 60V packs are separate systems.
A drive system the maker says gives 30% more torque. It helps the head keep turning in thick growth.
For big lawns and frequent use, yes. For small lawns a brushed motor is fine.

faq.q: How long will a battery last?
faq.a: It depends on pack size and growth. A 4.0Ah 24V pack lasts longer than a 2.0Ah 40V pack.
Use the diameter the head is rated for. The 60V takes 0.095 inch and the 24V 13 inch 0.080 inch.
